Grepping the whole painter directory for unit arithmetic finds only bls_spectrum_painter.dart:153-154, which is the x-AXIS tick label (h below one day, d above) and is now honestly captioned 'Period (h / d, log)' at :166; the LS axis is 'Frequency (1/day)'. The three numeric inputs are explicitly '(d)' (:316, :338, :400) and the 'Searched X-Y d' provenance line carries its own ' d' suffix (:730-732), so nothing else on the card states a period in an unlabelled or conflicting unit. title: Image grader shows the same value 'off' with the slider thumb at opposite ends of two adjacent tracks
repairSummary: Repair was already landed by the prior verify pass and I confirmed it is real and load-bearing, not just described: minRuleThumbValue(int?, int, int) exists beside maxRuleThumbValue in image_grader_dialog.dart:600-604 and is used at the _IntRow call site (:737), so a Min rule's thumb now follows the widened track instead of clamping to rangeMax. Backed by unit assertions (minRuleThumbValue(701, 700, 700) == 701) and a widget test that opens the grader on a SINGLE frame (every range degenerate) with a persisted minStars of 701 and asserts the Min-stars Slider.value is 701.
reasoning: The fixer's own diagnosis was right -- 'the off value was clamped against rangeMax, i.e. to the BOTTOM of a track that runs one unit higher' -- and they fixed only _DoubleRow. _IntRow, the adjacent row in the same widget, kept `(value ?? rangeMin).clamp(rangeMin, rangeMax)` against a Slider whose max was already thresholdSliderMax(...). An OFF Min-stars rule was unaffected (rangeMin is inside both ranges), which is why the shipped tests passed, but a SET Min stars rule on a degenerate range -- which is EVERY range whenever the grader is opened on one frame -- sprang the thumb back to rangeMin while the readout kept the higher number. That is the same thumb-disagrees-with-readout defect, left in the neighbouring row, hence INCOMPLETE rather than HOLDS. I re-severed the repair to prove it is wired. Two residuals I am recording but did not repair, because both are outside this finding (which is about OFF rules) and repairing the second would mean rewriting an assertion the fixer wrote deliberately: (a) the literal reported picture survives BY DESIGN -- an off 'Max' rule parks at the top and an off 'Min stars' rule at the bottom, so three adjacent rows can still read 'off' with the middle thumb at the opposite end; the fixer's permissive-end convention plus the 0.45-opacity dimming is a defensible reading and the dimming is a real visual change (Opacity does not block hit testing, so the track stays draggable, which is how an off rule is switched on), not a label; (b) a SET rule whose persisted value lies outside the session's observed range is still clamped to the track edge while the readout shows the true number -- a saved maxHfr of 4.0 opened on a session whose HFRs are all 1.8-2.2 shows the thumb hard right with the readout '4.00 px'. The existing test encodes that as intended (`maxRuleThumbValue(99.0, 0.0, 12.0) == 12.0`), so it is a design compromise rather than an accident, but it is the same shape and worth a decision.
evidence: SEVER: reverting image_grader_dialog.dart:737 to `final effective = (value ?? rangeMin).clamp(rangeMin, rangeMax);` makes image_grader_off_rule_test.dart red -- 'Expected: <701> Actual: <700.0>' on 'a set Min stars rule keeps its thumb where its readout says'. Restored; the file is green at '+12: All tests passed!' (run together with the wizard picker file). Call-site inventory: _DoubleRow serves only Max rules (Max HFR / Max FWHM / Max eccentricity / Max guiding RMS) and _IntRow only Min stars, so the permissive-end convention has no third case to get wrong.

title: Photometric Calibration Wizard's frame picker has no select-all / filter-by-altitude, so building the airmass spread it asks for means clicking through 120 identical rows
repairSummary: Repair already landed by the prior verify pass and confirmed load-bearing here: 'Select all usable' now anchors the filter the way a first frame tap does (frame_selection.dart:267-286) -- with the Filter field still empty it adopts the first usable frame's filter, writes it into _filterController so the user can see and change it, and then selects only the frames matching it. Guarded by a widget test that opens the wizard on a V/V/B session with no filter chosen and asserts '2 of 3 selected - 1 unusable' plus 'V' in the Filter field.
reasoning: Everything the summary claims is present: airmassForFrame (frame_selection.dart:437-438) wraps the product's airmassForTrueAltitude, each row carries 'Alt 52.3 deg - X 1.26' or 'no recorded altitude - cannot fit' in colors.warning (:337-368, :418-423), and the header shows 'N of M selected - K unusable' with 'Select all usable' and 'Clear' (:240-297). star_matching.dart:279-293 really does throw on a null airmass rather than assuming X = 1.0, using the IDENTICAL predicate (null altitude, else airmassForTrueAltitude), so the picker's usable set and the fit genuinely agree. The gap was the path the fixer never exercised: the wizard opens with _filterName = '' (photometric_calibration_wizard.dart:65), _filterMismatches returns false while that is empty (:314-320), so on a freshly opened wizard one click on 'Select all usable' selected EVERY solved frame in the session including other filters -- and the tap path then refuses those same frames with a snackbar. The fixer's own test taps a V frame first, pre-anchoring the filter, so it never saw it. The summary's 'so it cannot hand the fit a frame it will reject' was therefore false on the default path. Everything else stands up: _changeFilter clears the selection whenever the filter is edited (:149-163), a session change clears it too (:118-126), and setting _filterController.text programmatically does not re-enter onChanged, so the anchoring cannot loop. The declined items (sort-by-airmass, spread picker) are honestly disclosed, and the residual refusals the picker cannot predict (fewer than 4 stars from a fresh measureStars pass) genuinely need the frame measured first. One residual, not repaired: once a filter is anchored, the header's 'K unusable' conflates 'wrong filter' with 'no recorded altitude', so a V calibration on a B+V+R session reports the other filters as unusable without saying why.
evidence: SEVER: with the anchoring in place, reverting the selection to `..addAll(usable.map((img) => img.id))` makes photometric_wizard_frame_picker_test.dart red -- 'Found 0 widgets with text "2 of 3 selected - 1 unusable"' on 'Select all anchors the filter when none has been chosen yet'. Restored; green at '+12: All tests passed!' including all five original picker tests.

title: Calibration wizard prints solved RA/Dec as bare decimals with no unit
reasoning: Verified end to end. captured_images.solved_ra really is HOURS: science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:523 writes `solvedRa: solved.raHours` through updatePlateSolveResult, and star_matching.dart:312 reads it straight back as WcsSolution.raHours, so the fixer's correction of the finding's '120.0000 deg' expectation is right and the reporter's value was seeded test data in an hours column. Both display sites now go through the core formatters -- frame_selection.dart:363-364 and frame_detail_dialog.dart:229-230 -- and CoordinateParser.formatRaHms / formatDecDms (coordinate_parser.dart:174-186, :188-194) emit 'HH:MM:SS.ss' / '+DD:MM:SS.ss' with NaN/infinite guards. A grep for solvedRa/solvedDec across skotiq_app finds no remaining analytics surface printing a bare decimal; centering_dialog and the polar-alignment measurement panel format their own, separate, live plate-solve state. The widget test asserts the rendered 'RA 05:30:00.00' / 'Dec +25:00:00.00' through the real PhotometricCalibrationWizard and asserts the old 'RA: 5.5000' finds nothing, so the production call site is covered by construction and a sever was unnecessary. One sub-claim in the summary is wrong and worth recording: 'a degrees-valued seed would now be visibly out of range' is false -- formatRaHms folds its input into [0, 24) (coordinate_parser.dart:180-184), so a 120 written into the hours column renders as an innocuous '00:00:00.00'. That does not affect the defect being fixed. frame_detail_dialog's copy of the formatting has no test of its own.
evidence: photometric_wizard_frame_picker_test.dart 'RA is printed in hours, sexagesimally, not as a bare decimal' passes against the real wizard. Writer/reader chain: private_helpers.dart:521-523 (write raHours) -> star_matching.dart:312 (read as raHours). Fold that refutes the out-of-range sub-claim: coordinate_parser.dart:180-184.

title: With no data at all, Analytics > Session invents a session card called "Quick Capture" instead of an empty state
reasoning: The gate is real and correctly narrow. analytics_screen/session_tab.dart:171-175 computes noStandaloneFrames only when the tab is in standalone mode AND the standalone stream has already resolved to an empty list, so a loading or errored stream still falls through to the existing 'Loading...' / 'Unavailable' paths (:210-215) rather than flashing an empty state. isLive and isStandaloneMode are provably mutually exclusive (isLive requires sessionState.dbSessionId == reviewSessionId and reviewSessionId is null in standalone mode, :39-45), so a live run can never be hidden behind the empty state. Both branches exist as described (:181-230): with no sessions it reuses l10n analyticsNoSessionHistory / analyticsNoSessionHistoryDesc -- existing keys, the same pair the History tab uses, so no new untranslated strings -- and with sessions on record it keeps the _SessionReviewBar and says 'No quick captures' / 'Choose a session above to review it.', which is true and actionable where 'you have not imaged yet' would be a lie. Nothing else in the app fabricates the card: the only other 'Quick Capture' strings are the flat wizard tab, two sequencer templates and the imaging capture panel's link INTO this bucket. The tests drive the real AnalyticsScreen, not the sub-widget.
evidence: SEVER: forcing `noStandaloneFrames` false makes session_tab_empty_state_test.dart red on two of three tests -- 'Expected: no matching candidates / Actual: Found 1 widget with text "Quick Capture"' for both the no-data profile and the sessions-on-record case. Restored; green at '+3: All tests passed!'.

title: Empty-chart messages splice the axis label into the sentence, producing "No °C recorded for these frames"
reasoning: session_chart.dart:39 adds the optional measurementName beside yAxisLabel; :75 composes the empty state as `'No ${measurementName ?? title.toLowerCase()} recorded for these frames'`, so a future chart that forgets the parameter still gets a noun phrase rather than a unit. All four wrappers pass one: 'half-flux radius' (:414), 'sensor temperature' (:440), 'guiding RMS' (:466), 'focuser position' (:495). SessionChart has exactly one definition and exactly four production call sites, all in this file, so there is no fifth copy of the bug; the unit-bearing yAxisLabel is still used where units belong (axis caption and point tooltip). A grep for an interpolated 'No $...' sentence across skotiq_app and skotiq_ui returns no other site. The tests build the production wrappers rather than SessionChart directly.
evidence: SEVER: dropping `measurementName: 'half-flux radius'` from HfrChart makes session_chart_empty_label_test.dart red -- 'Found 0 widgets with text "No half-flux radius recorded for these frames"'. Restored; green at '+7'. Recorded, not a defect: severing TemperatureChart's measurementName does NOT go red, because its title is already 'Sensor temperature' so the fallback yields the identical sentence -- that one call site is redundant rather than unguarded, and behaviour is unchanged either way.
